extracted.intended_audience: NLP/ML researchers and practitioners studying peer review, dataset builders, and developers of LLM-based review/annotation tools
extracted.subtask_description: Deriving and using a taxonomy of review 'aspects' to (1) annotate review sentences, (2) build datasets of aspect-labeled peer-review text, and (3) train/evaluate models that predict which aspects a paper/review addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology (coarse aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodology as a top-level aspect covering Method, Model, Training, Approach, Parameter, Computational Complexity, Theoretical Substantiation, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to label sentences that evaluate the paper's methods (e.g., model architecture, training regime, computational complexity) or theory. Table 9 shows Methodology appears in ~34% of sentences; fine labels include Model, Method, Training, Approach, Parameter. Example anti-pattern: conflating 'Methodology' with 'Results' or 'Presentation'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Result / Performance (coarse aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspects concerning experimental results, improvement, performance, accuracy, robustness, experimental significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers evaluation outcomes and claims about empirical gains. Fine labels include Performance, Results, Experimental Results, Accuracy, Robustness. Use when a sentence discusses measured outcomes, statistical/significance concerns, or practical significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data / Task (coarse aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspects related to datasets, tasks, benchmarks, annotation, and data suitability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label sentences that mention dataset construction, task definition, dataset quality, or benchmark appropriateness. Fine labels include Dataset, Datasets, Tasks, Task, Data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation (coarse aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspects about clarity, figures, tables, typos, writing quality, readability, and overall presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for comments on clarity/formatting/visualization. Table 9 reports Presentation ~9.68% of sentences; top fine labels: Clarity, Presentation, Figure, Table, Typo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison (coarse aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspects addressing baselines, comparability, and comparative analysis with prior work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to sentences that critique or request comparisons to important baselines (e.g., missing P-tuning v2). Fine labels include Comparison, Baseline. Use when a paper lacks adequate comparative experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiment (coarse aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspects specifically about experimental setup, experimental design, or existence of experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label sentences that refer to experiments as a whole (experimental setup, number of trials, reproducibility). Table 9 lists 'Experiment' as a coarse aspect (examples and frequency shown).

rubrics_metrics.name: DDDDEI (Definition/Description/Detail/Discussion/Explanation/Interpretability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspects covering definition, explanation, description, detail, discussion, interpretability and explainability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when a sentence addresses need for definitions, detailed descriptions, or interpretable analyses. The paper used DDDDEI as a coarse aspect with fine labels like Explanation, Discussion, Definition, Description, Detail; also used under Explainability/Interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related Work / References
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspects concerning prior work coverage, citations, and reference completeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply when reviewers comment on missing related work, incorrect citations, or insufficient positioning relative to literature. Table 9 lists Related Work as a coarse category with fine labels like Reference, Related Work, Previous Work, Citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation (coarse aspect and metrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspects about evaluation methodology, choice of metrics, human evaluation, and empirical evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label sentences that comment on whether the evaluation is adequate, correct metrics were used, or human evaluation is required. Fine labels include Evaluation, Metric, Human Evaluation, Empirical Evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: IJMV (Intuition/Justification/Motivation/Validation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspects related to paper motivation, justification, intuition, and validation of claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for comments that probe why the work is done, whether motivation is sufficient, or if claims are validated. Fine labels include Motivation, Justification, Validation, Intuition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis (coarse aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspects for analytical work such as theoretical analysis, error analysis, qualitative/quantitative analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply to sentences offering analytical critique or requiring deeper analysis. Fine labels include Analysis, Theoretical Analysis, Error Analysis, Qualitative Analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspects addressing innovation, novelty, originality, and technical novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when a reviewer assesses whether the contribution is novel or incremental. Paper reports Novelty as a coarse label (fine labels: Novelty, Innovation/Novelty/Originality, Technical Novelty).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspects pertaining to the paper's central contributions and technical contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label sentences that summarize, question, or evaluate the main contributions. Fine labels: Contribution, Contributions, Technical Contribution, Main Contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance / Importance / Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspects that evaluate the broader importance, impact, or relevance of the problem and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when reviewers discuss problem importance, potential impact, or significance of results. Table 15 shows weaker agreement for Significance and Presentation in annotation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ablation / Ablation Study
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspects calling for or reporting ablation studies and component-wise analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label sentences that request or document ablation experiments. Fine labels include Ablation, Ablation Studies, Abalations Experiments; Table 9 shows frequency and association with Methodology/Experiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspects related to theoretical results, theorems, and theoretical substantiation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply to sentences critiquing theoretical rigor or requesting proofs/derivations. Fine labels: Theory, Theoretical Analysis, Theoretical Results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explainability / Interpretability
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspects demanding interpretable analyses, explanations, or natural-language rationales for results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when reviewers ask for visual/interpretability analyses or natural-language statements explaining model behavior. Fine labels include Explainability/Explanation, Interpretability/Interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification / Clarity / Writing Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspects that request clarification, improved exposition, or note poor writing quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label sentences that identify unclear passages, confusing experiments, or requests for rewriting. Fine labels listed include Clarification/Clarity, Writing Quality, Readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparability / Comparisons to baselines
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspects focused on ensuring experimental comparability and adequate baselines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when a reviewer notes missing baselines or non-standard comparisons (e.g., missing P-tuning v2). Fine labels: Comparability/Comparison, Baselines, Model Comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metrics used for consistency between LLM annotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use BERTScore and Jaccard similarity (and thresholds like BERTScore ≥ 0.9) to quantify consistency between annotation sets; also report raw exact match rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper reports consistency scores between different prompts/temperatures using raw annotations and mapped COARSE labels (Table 10). Use these automatic similarity metrics to evaluate annotation consistency across LLM settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation screening criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruit annotators with graduate/doctorate degrees in Computer Science, native English speakers, approval rate > 90% on Prolific; run pilot studies and select a small set (3 annotators in this study).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to ensure annotation quality. Also sample review sentences to maintain class balance and require annotators to provide explanations to mitigate automation bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human annotation protocol: require explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: When asking humans to validate LLM annotations, require annotators to give textual explanations for their judgments to mitigate automation bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces the chance that annotators simply confirm the LLM output. The paper followed Fabbri et al. (2021) setup and required explanations; questionnaire examples and counts (3032 entries) are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-annotator agreement measurement (Fleiss' Kappa)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure inter-annotator reliability using Fleiss' Kappa and monitor agreement over annotation ranges (e.g., first N entries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper reports Fleiss' Kappas for different prefix ranges (e.g., κ=0.4739 for first 600 entries, overall κ=0.1944), and flags annotation quality decline over time as an operational concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-processing LLM annotations workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-stage post-processing: automated categorization using high-frequency terms and frequency thresholds to remove low-frequency terms; manual expert verification of remaining terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper reports the automated part and that manual verification took ~10 hours for one expert. This is recommended as a reproducible pipeline for mapping raw LLM outputs into a domain taxonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxonomy construction requires domain expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructing an aspect taxonomy requires mapping post-processed annotations into domain-relevant evaluation dimensions using expert judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper reports taxonomy construction required ~72 hours of expert effort. Emphasizes that taxonomy design is non-trivial and should reflect domain evaluation needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt design and LLM sensitivity checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Design prompts (e.g., Table 7) that ask the LLM to output JSON with identified aspects; test sensitivity by substituting synonyms ('aspect' → 'facet') and varying temperature (e.g., temperature in {0,1}) and seeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format the LLM output as JSON dictionaries for structured post-processing. Perform validity checks across prompt wording and decoding settings to measure annotation stability (consistency tables provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental reporting and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Report all experimental settings (model types, hyperparameters, seeds, epochs, batch sizes, learning rates) and the seed used for LLM queries; acknowledge reproducibility limits for closed-weight LLMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper provides settings for RandomForest (n_estimators=100), RoBERTa (batch_size=16, learning_rate=3e-5, 10 epochs), GPT-4o (temperature=0, seed=2266). Note concerns about exact reproducibility when using closed models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of modeling formulation for PAP (aspect prediction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design choice: treat PAP as binary classification (which aspects to focus on) vs modeling as ranking or regression to reflect different importance levels of aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper treated PAP as binary for simplicity but notes that ranking/regression may better match real-world needs where aspects have different weights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling strategy and class-balance in annotation
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample review sentences to maintain class balance as much as possible when creating annotation sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper sampled 100 reviews corresponding to 1852 sentences and aimed for balanced aspect distributions (see Table 13). This mitigates skew in training/evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical guideline: tool to assist, not replace, human reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: LLM-generated aspect prediction and review-assistance tools are intended to assist reviewers, not replace human judgment; reviewers retain autonomy to include suggested aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since data used are anonymized and public, processing with commercial LLMs is not deemed ethically problematic, but automation bias and selection biases must be considered and mitigated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias and dataset-selection caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge selection biases: use of camera-ready versions, class imbalance (e.g., many accepted papers), and their impact on aspect frequency and downstream use of aspect sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper warns that bias may overestimate certain aspect frequencies; recommends more diverse review data to mitigate these biases before using aspect sets to inform review forms/guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics for model/task performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Report precision, recall, F1, and Jaccard similarity for aspect prediction and related tasks; use appropriate evaluation splits (e.g., 90/10 train/test).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper presents detailed tables for BoW+RF, RoBERTa, GPT-4o across inputs (full paper, abstract, title, keywords) and label granularities (COARSE/FINE). Use few-shot/zero-shot distinctions for LLM evaluations.
